messages:
anya: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a rollforward (incremental) to move the controlplane connector inside customer VPCs instead of full peering. want to capture operational risks we may have missed and get buy-in for the canary plan.
liam: +1 to incremental. main concern: route churn and accidental default-route leaks during cutover. how are we preventing propagated 0.0.0.0/0 or broad CIDR import?
maya: agreed. we should filter route propagation aggressively. plan sketch: create a per-tenant route map that only advertises specific CP prefixes and next-hop via the connector ENI. nothing else.
liam: example filter i was thinking (cloud-provider pseudo):
```
route-map rm-cp-allow permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list CP-PREFIXES
 set community no-export
! prefix-list CP-PREFIXES permit 10.11.12.0/24
```
this prevents accidental wide routes.
david: also need to think about SNAT. when we shift egress path to customer VPC, we must preserve source IP for customer-side firewall rules or they'll break. are we doing source-preservation or will we SNAT to connector ENI?
anya: goal is preserve src if possible. but ops pointed out cross-account IP preservation is hard with some cloud providers. fallback is SNAT with mapping table + sticky sessions.
maya: another ops risk: cert propagation for workload-auth between CP and dataplane. if we flip connectors, we need a safe rollout for cert rotation. suggestion: use short-lived proxy tokens and have fallback polling to controlplane fallback endpoints in our region if handshake fails.
liam: DNS split-horizon question: customers will often expect private endpoints at edge.example.com -> internal IP. during cutover we may have split answers. propose TTL 0 for canary window and health-check-driven promotion.
david: we should also rate-limit controlplane handshake retries during migration to avoid token storms. add circuit-breaker at connector side.
anya: ops checklist I'm thinking to include:
- create strict route filters (no default/large CIDRs)
- enable srcip-preserve where supported, else enable SNAT mapping service
- deploy cert-rotation plan with canary timers
- set DNS TTL=0 for cutover window + health checks
- implement handshake retry throttling + exponential backoff
- rollback path: revert route advertise and drain connector ENI

maya: one more low-level: port exhaustion on NAT if we SNAT many tenants through shared connector. if we do per-tenant SNAT pool, that'll increase IP usage but gives headroom. otherwise ephemeral ports will be exhausted quickly for high-throughput tenants.
liam: yep. for shared connectors we should monitor ephemeral port utilization metric and have an autoscale policy that adds ENIs before we hit 75% port usage. alerting threshold + automatic relaunch.
sre-bot: deploy-check: connector-filter-policy v2 applied to beta-tenant-3 at 1711304500 — no errors reported.
anya: thanks @sre-bot — looks good. next question: canary cutover order — do we prefer "attach connector then switch DNS" or "switch DNS then attach"?
david: attach first. gives observability and ability to fail fast. after connector shows healthy, shift small % of DNS traffic then ramp.
maya: agree. attach -> healthchecks -> dns shift -> monitor 15m -> ramp. keep rollback <10m target.
liam: small PR sketch for routing automation:
```json
{
 "tenant": "beta-3",
 "allowed_prefixes": ["10.11.12.0/24"],
 "snat_profile": "preserve-if-supported",
 "dns_ttl_cutover": 0
}
```
not final but enough for infra to test.
anya: action items:
- @liam: write route-filter puppet module and canary playbook (due EOD friday)
- @maya: verify cert-rotation fallback and token TTLs with auth team (due monday)
- @david: define SNAT pool autoscale alert + run port-exhaustion sim (due next wednesday)
- ops: schedule canary tenant and window (ops@)

liam: noted. i'll push a branch and tag ppl for review.
maya: i'll sync with auth and post follow-up here.
david: will run a short sim and post numbers.
anya: thanks all. i’ll draft the migration runbook and ping infra for a dry-run next week. :thumbsup:
